pool.text: A convex \( 6 \)-gon has no three diagonals concurrent at an interior point. How many interior intersection points are formed by its diagonals?

pool.sol: Every \( 4 \)-element subset of the \( 6 \) vertices forms a unique convex quadrilateral whose two diagonals cross at a unique interior point. By this bijection, the number of interior diagonal intersections is \( \binom{6}{4} = 15 \).
hints: Notice that each interior diagonal crossing uses \( 2 \) diagonals, hence \( 4 \) polygon vertices.
Every \( 4 \) vertices of a convex polygon determine exactly \( 1 \) pair of crossing diagonals.

pool.sol: Every \( 4 \)-element subset of the \( 16 \) vertices forms a unique convex quadrilateral whose two diagonals cross at a unique interior point. By this bijection, the number of interior diagonal intersections is \( \binom{16}{4} = 1820 \).
hints: Notice that each interior diagonal crossing uses \( 2 \) diagonals, hence \( 4 \) polygon vertices.
Every \( 4 \) vertices of a convex polygon determine exactly \( 1 \) pair of crossing diagonals.
Substitute your simplified expression into the target condition and verify signs and domain restrictions.

pool.text: Olympiad Proof Investigation (Bijective Counting, Inclusion-Exclusion & Pigeonhole): Let \( n \ge 1 \) be an integer and consider \( P(n) = n^3 + 18n^2 + 107n \).
pool.educational_aim: Master Bijective Counting, Inclusion-Exclusion & Pigeonhole via authentic Olympiad, NSMO of KSA, and KAUST KMC problem-solving (easy tier).
pool.sol: (a) \( P(1) = 126 \), and \( P(n) + 216 = (n+6)^3 - n \). (b) For \( k = n+6 \), \( k^3 - k = (k-1)k(k+1) \) is a product of three consecutive integers, hence divisible by \( 6 \). (c) Setting \( n = 6k \) makes every term of \( P(6k) \) a multiple of \( 6 \), giving remainder \( 0 \).

pool.text: [KAUST Thuwal Finals] Let \( \zeta = e^{2\pi i / 5} \) be a primitive \( 5 \)-th root of unity (plotted on the Argand diagram). Evaluate the exact complex product \[ \prod_{k=1}^{4} \left(2 - \zeta^k\right). \]
pool.educational_aim: Master KAUST Campus Finals & Academy Advanced Synthesis via authentic Olympiad, NSMO of KSA, and KAUST KMC problem-solving (easy tier).
pool.sol: Because \( 1, \zeta, \zeta^2, \dots, \zeta^{4} \) are all \( 5 \) roots of \( z^{5} - 1 \), dividing out \( (z - 1) \) yields the cyclotomic identity \[ \prod_{k=1}^{4} (z - \zeta^k) = \frac{z^{5} - 1}{z - 1} = 1 + z + \dots + z^{4}. \] Substituting \( z = 2 \) gives \( 31 \).
hints: Identify \( \prod_{k=1}^{4}(z - \zeta^k) = 1 + z + z^2 + \dots + z^{4} \).

pool.sol: Let \( P(x) = (1 + x)^{6} \). hints: Average \( \omega^{-0k}(1 + \omega^k)^{6} \) over \( k = 0, 1, 2 \) where \( 1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0 \).
Replace \( 1 + \omega = -\omega^2 = e^{i\pi/3} \) and \( 1 + \omega^2 = -\omega = e^{-i\pi/3} \).
